alex_g: Heads-up — we're seeing a ~3x Xid spike in eu-west since the kernel + driver roll at 02:10. Pattern looks different: spikes align with heavy network egress bursts. Anybody else seeing a netlink/PCIe correlation? maria_ops: Confirmed on a handful of hosts. dmesg shows PCIe link retrain around the same timestamps as Xid 31. jon.sweeney: That smells like the PCIe retimer firmware + NIC offload combo. We've hit similar once when NIC offload caused microbursts that retrained links and triggered GPU driver timeouts. sre-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-rollout eu-west completed at 02:10 (version 6.1.15-redwood.4). devon_r: Quick checks: can someone paste `dmesg | grep -i xid` and `ethtool -k ` from affected hosts? Also collect PM logs + `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=uuid,pstate,ecc.errors.uncorrected.memory --format=csv` alex_g: Pasted sample from host gw-eu-12:``` [ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=2879, name=python [ 12345.679200] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: PME: Failed to assert
[ 12345.680123] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0 NIC: link training completed, speed 16GT/s ``` kai-lin: ethtool shows `rx-checksumming: on` and `sg: on` on the Mellanox NICs. Try disabling large offloads (esp GRO/TSO) on canary hosts to see if spikes drop. maria_ops: Standing up a quick canary: disabling GSO/TSO/GRO on 3 hosts and running the synthetic load that repros. jon.sweeney: Also add PCIe ASPM/logging toggles: set `pcie_aspm=off` for a test kernel boot on one canary node. If retrains stop, we isolate to link power-management. alex_g: Cost/ops note: draining 3 cards for deeper burn-in costs ~2hrs of capacity and ~0.12 GPU-days. We can limit to lower-priority pools. Thoughts? :money_with_wings: devon_r: Fine to use preemptible capacity from staging for tests. If we need a larger sample, schedule a gradual drain with tc limits so we don't impact prod much. maria_ops: Canary results so far (30m): disabled offloads hosts = Xid count 0, baseline hosts = 8 spikes. Looks promising. jon.sweeney: If this holds, plan: (1) rollback NIC FW/enable safe offload config across eu-west, (2) add a kernel flag to nightly kernel images to opt-out of ASPM, (3) run targeted burnin with network stress for 24h, (4) patch the driver to increase timeout tolerance for retrain events. kai-lin: I'll prepare a monitoring dashboard: correlate `net.if.egress_bytes`, `pcie.link_retrain_count`, and `gpu.xid_rate` per host. Need feed names. alex_g: Assigning owners: maria_ops -> run expanded canary + collect logs; jon.sweeney -> driver timeout proposal; kai-lin -> dashboard; devon_r -> capacity plan and drain playbook. I'll coordinate with infra to gate any rollbacks. maria_ops: Quick reproduction commands I'm running on canary:```bash # network tx load iperf3 -c -P 8 -t 600 -b 0 # collect logs dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.log etstat -s > /tmp/netstat.log etperf -H ``` jon.sweeney: Add `sudo pciehp_poll_disable` and `echo 0 > /sys/module/pcie_aspm/parameters/policy` toggles for the ASPM test. alex_g: If we see replicated behaviour, we'll hold kernel rollouts in eu-west and open a hotfix branch for the driver. Please ping #incidents if Xid spikes resume outside canary. sre-bot: incident-bot: created INC-2024-2415 for eu-west gpu-xid-spike; severity=low -> monitoring escalations configured. maria_ops: Update: after disabling GSO/GRO/TSO on 6 hosts, 12h zero Xid. I'll upload artifacts to the incident ticket and add host lists. devon_r: Sounds like a plan. Let's also coordinate with networking to verify retimer FW versions and check for recent NIC firmware pushes around the kernel rollout window. alex_g: Great work all. Next sync in 2h; if anyone sees regressions, react in-thread and we'll pause the rollouts. :thumbsup:
